name: Primary Oculocerebral Lymphoma
aliases: Primary Intraocular Lymphoma with CNS Involvement
Primary Central Nervous System Lymphoma with Ocular Manifestations

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Diagnostic Criteria for Primary Oculocerebral Lymphoma

criteria.description: Histopathological confirmation of lymphoma cells in ocular or CNS tissue
MRI evidence of enhancing lesions in the brain and/or ocular structures consistent with lymphoma
Cerebrospinal fluid cytology showing malignant lymphoid cells or positive flow cytometry
Presence of characteristic neurological and ophthalmological symptoms without systemic lymphoma evidence

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation plus MRI evidence and compatible clinical presentation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis often requires combined ophthalmologic, neurologic, and pathological evaluation.

pathognomonic.notes: Presence of malignant lymphoid cells in vitreous humor
searchTerms: eye inflammation with abnormal lymphoid cells

pathognomonic.symptomName: Focal neurological deficits related to CNS lymphoma lesions
searchTerms: localized neurological problems from brain lymphoma
focal nerve deficits due to CNS lymphoma

pathognomonic.symptomName: Subretinal infiltrates with retinal pigment epithelium disruption
searchTerms: lesions under retina with pigment disruption
retinal pigment epithelium damage with infiltrates

common.symptomName: Visual disturbances including blurred vision and floaters
searchTerms: visual disturbances with spots in vision
pain in head related to intracranial mass

common.symptomName: Diplopia due to cranial nerve involvement

occasional.symptomName: Seizures secondary to cerebral lymphoma involvement
Nausea and vomiting related to increased intracranial pressure

searchTerms: ptosis due to cranial nerve damage

rare.symptomName: Systemic B symptoms (fever, night sweats, weight loss)
rare.notes: Uncommon in primary CNS lymphoma without systemic spread
searchTerms: general body symptoms like fever and sweating

laboratory: CSF cytology positive for malignant lymphoid cells
Elevated interleukin-10 levels in vitreous or CSF
Flow cytometry demonstrating clonal B-cell population
imaging: MRI showing homogeneously enhancing lesions in periventricular white matter or deep brain structures
Ocular coherence tomography (OCT) revealing subretinal infiltrates
Fluorescein angiography showing retinal pigment epithelium abnormalities
genetic: Frequent MYD88 L265P mutation in tumor cells
other: Elevated protein and lymphocytic pleocytosis in CSF

distinguishingFeatures: Predominantly CNS lesions without vitreous infiltration

redFlags: Failure to respond to corticosteroid therapy
references: Chan CC, et al. Primary intraocular lymphoma: diagnosis and treatment. Int Ophthalmol Clin. 2018.
Batchelor TT, et al. Primary CNS lymphoma. J Clin Oncol. 2019.
